Gathers relationships for narrative entities.
A location specified or implied by the narrative.

note.value: These can be real (e.g., a documentary comparing Soho in London to Soho in New York), fictionalized real (e.g., The White House, as it exists in the narrative), or completely imaginary (e.g., Tatooine.)

definition.en: A real place that is used when producing the Creative Work.

example.value: Sound Stage 3 can be used to create the depiction of 'MegaCorp boardroom', and the estate at West Wycombe Park is used to depict some locations in Pride and Prejudice and Zombies.

definition.en: A Prop as specified or implied by the narrative.
An Asset used in the Depiction of a Narrative Prop.
The clothing for a Character in the narrative.
A series of images that forms a visual representation of some part of the narrative.
A moving image produced from the individual images of a Storyboard.
Images or other material used to inform the artistic aspects of creation of a production, to help convey a tone or look, etc.
Images, documents, data, or other material created as part of the execution of the production.
Taken from the narrative itself and traditionally defined by creative intent and various kinds of unity (e.g., time, place, action, or theme).
A sentient entity (usually a person but not always) in the script whose specific identity is consequential to the narrative. A Character is generally identified by a specific name.
An exploratory representation of something from the narrative.

note.value: Concept covers anything that is used or created as input to the final depiction of a narrative element in the Creative Work, including storyboards, concept art, costume ideas, possible filming locations, and so on.

definition.en: Images that illustrate ideas for potential depictions of elements of the creative intent.
The representation of a Narrative Entity (See Part 2A: Narrative Elements) by a production entity in the Creative Work, specified or implied by the Script.
The Depiction of a Character.
A uniquely identified production.
The number of the day on the filming schedule.
An ordered collection of media used to organize units of work.

note.value: A collection and grouping mechanism, usually associated with a scope of work

definition.en: A Sequence of Editorial Shots linked to creative intent.

note.value: Typically has a close relationship to narrative intent

definition.en: A Shot that has been identified as requiring VFX work.
A unit of work made up of an ordered series of VFX shots.

note.value: May not be a continuous narrative

definition.en: A Shot that has been identified as requiring Animation work.
A unit of work made up of an ordered series of Animation shots.

note.value: Shots with both live action and animation would be a VFX Shot

definition.en: A sequence of shots with color grading characteristics linked to creative intent.
A physical asset is one where the tangible reality of the Asset is its defining feature.
Information that exists as digital data.
An Asset Structure composed of digital data.
A two-dimensional visual representation.
A temporally ordered sequence of Images
A representation of sound.
A human readable object containing text and/or images.
A Document structured according to a set of rules which are used to parse or understand the document.
Describes the use or purpose of an Asset within the production process.
Look up table

note.value: A look up table is an array, either two or three dimensional, that changes the way an image looks. For example, a LUT can be used to transform an image from one color space to another

definition.en: Describes how a series of Shots is used to generate a Sequence.
A predefined encoding for communicating color appearance.
A discrete unit of visual narrative with a specified beginning and end.
A Structured Document written as a blueprint to convey the creative intent for the Creative Work. Parsing the Script generates a guide to those things that are to be depicted in production.
The result of recording any event by any means.
An Image Sequence used in VFX work.
A temporally ordered sequence of individual images which are the constituent parts of a Moving Image.
Effects created on or in the footage after it is captured.

note.value: Has Participant Structural Class of Organization

definition.en: A Moving Image with Audio synchronized to the images.
Identifier for a group of events captured together on the same camera and recording media.
Capture-specific details and information about the Lens itself.
Information about a Recorder and the recording media.
A fixed, specified physical Location used for shooting/filming the production.

example.value: Sound Stage 3 can be used to create the depiction of 'MegaCorp boardroom', and the estate at West Wycombe Park is used to depict some locations in Pride and Prejudice and Zombies.

definition.en: Capture-specific details and information about the Camera itself.
The recording of motion as a stream of digital data.
Final Audio Assets and Compositions combined based on their Audio Classification, used to produce the final sound for the Creative Work in a particular Soundfield.
An Asset Structure that produces data that does not persist outside of its immediate use.
A configuration file for a color management system.
A shape defined in three dimensions.
An image intended to drive or influence a behavior or value within a CG workflow.
Data values and relationships required to describe the look of a CG Asset.
A Material represented by a Composition.
A Composition that includes a collection of related CG Assets and CG Assemblies.
A Composition containing only Geometry information.
A sentient entity (usually a person, but not always) in the Script whose specific identity is minimally consequential to the narrative.
A significant tangible thing in the narrative.
Plant material and terrain-building material described or implied in the narrative,

note.value: this covers living plants (potted ferns, planted trees, fields of daffodils, etc.) and cut plants (e.g. single flowers, daisy chains, and sprigs of mistletoe) as well as rocks, sand, etc.

definition.en: An Asset or Assets used to depict Narrative greenery in a Production Scene.
Any mode of transport specified or implied by the narrative.
An Asset used in the Depiction of a Narrative Vehicle
Hair requirements, procuring and maintaining wigs, and styling and cutting the hair of Participants in Portrayals.
Application and Maintenance of make-up for anyone appearing on-screen.
The use of molding, casting, and sculpting techniques to create the required look for a Character.
A significant sound in the narrative.
A sound that explicitly or implicitly advances or supports the narrative.
Music that is implicitly or explicitly used to advance or support the narrative.
A technique that creates or enhances visual elements in the finished work
Physically based effects, such as explosions, the use of mannequins, and the use of models, the results of which are captured on-camera.
Physical action described or implied in the narrative that would put an actor in some kind of danger and so requires a specialist to manage and coordinate.
The creation, arrangement, and management of dance.
Anything involving work on water or in water-borne craft.
Anything involving work with equipment that flies.
Set Dressing as implied or specified by the narrative.
Assets used in the depiction of Narrative Set Dressing.
Action in a Narrative Scene that will require involving a specialist such as a Fight Coordinator in the production process.
Geometry built as input for a 3D printer process
3D elements that provide additional information or commentary on other geometry.
Geometry that acts as a background or underlay for visual atmosphere creation.
Geometry used as a visual guide or reference in animation and VFX.
Simplified geometry for collision detection and physics simulations.
Lower-resolution geometry used for faster pre-visualization and playback.
Final high-quality visual output of 3D geometry.
A group of Creative Works with a common overarching title and a strong relationship between the individual Creative Works.
A group of Episodes in a Series that are made or distributed together.
A single Creative Work that is part of Series or Season
Material created to support some other work, such as a trailer, featurette, deleted scenes, gag reel, interviews, behind-the-scenes, etc.
A feature film or other long-from motion picture that first appeared in theatrical exhibition or was released directly to video (home entertainment). If the duration is ≤ 40 minutes, then the record
Content that first appeared via broadcast (terrestrial, satellite, cable, etc.). This includes telefilms, other one-off programs, and Episodes of television series.
A short program (≤ 40 minutes) that first appeared in theatrical exhibition or was released directly to video (home entertainment). If the duration is > 40 minutes, then the record is a Movie.
Element of the narrative that directly influence the appearance of a Character, including hair, makeup, and prosthetics.
A generic use for Geometry.
Illustrations, photographs, or other materials that illustrate some aspect of a Creative Work.
A segment of audio essence with associated metadata describing positional and other properties which may vary with time.
A distinct collection of sequenced audio samples that are intended for delivery to a single loudspeaker or other reproduction device.
A temporally continuous sequence of related samples.
A combination of multiple Audio Assets and Compositions into a particular format.
A Composition consisting of audio assets, Audio Compositions, and an Audio Session.
The Channel component of an immersive STEM or Printmaster.
The combination of STEMs for a particular soundfield at unity gain.
Playable audio that can be packaged and distributed with a finished Creative Work.
An Asset used in the portrayal of a Character.
